llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed Android automation bridge, but it gives broad phone-control capability and has under-scoped network and screenshot-retention risks.

dimensions.detail: Appium is launched without an explicit loopback bind address, and screenshots are written to predictable /sdcard paths before being pulled, with no device-side cleanup found.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a local virtualenv and ordinary Python packages, but the documented pip install has unpinned dependencies and no integrity checks.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill documents explicit user consent before irreversible actions and says payment credentials stay user-entered, but its commands can still control any connected Android app once invoked.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: One-shot mode is documented as the safer default, but the opt-in launcher starts Appium and a background daemon and uses broad process matching to terminate bridge_daemon processes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The ability to read screens, use accessibility data, tap, scroll, type, and assist booking or checkout flows matches the stated Android-automation purpose, but it is inherently high impact.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving this skill broad control over a connected Android device. Prefer one-shot commands, avoid using it on sensitive screens unless necessary, clean screenshots after use, and bind Appium to loopback before running the daemon.
llm.findings:
[T05] unexpected: A local Appium server is purpose-aligned, but the artifact does not constrain the server bind address despite the server enabling powerful Android device control.
[T09] unexpected: Phone screenshots are expected for OCR, but fixed files under /sdcard are not deleted after pull, which exceeds the documented private host-side retention story.
[T08] unexpected: Third-party OCR and automation dependencies are expected, but resolving unpinned latest packages during install leaves the effective runtime code mutable.
[E2] expected: The environment is passed to the Appium subprocess; I found no artifact-backed external transmission or secret logging, so this is downgraded from exfiltration to ordinary subprocess inheritance.
[TM1] expected: The rm -f operations remove specific bridge IPC files in the skill cache directory and are consistent with cleanup, though the launcher also has separate overbroad pkill behavior.
[TM3] expected: The world-writable reference is part of a safety check rejecting group/world-writable IPC files, not an unsafe default.
[AST4] expected: Subprocess use is expected for launching Appium and running adb with argument lists; the main concern is service exposure and screenshot cleanup, not command injection evidence.
[AST3] expected: Dynamic imports only load the standard re module with a constant name and do not show arbitrary module loading.
[RA2] expected: The background daemon is disclosed and opt-in, not a startup hook or cross-session backdoor, but it still deserves user review because it keeps a live Android automation session.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The reported undefined driver in cmd_ocr_tap appears to be a functional defect rather than malicious behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Host-side screenshots are disclosed and stored in a private directory with age-based cleanup, but users should treat them as sensitive local artifacts.
